signatures.name: tit_for_tat_reciprocity_pd
signatures.description: In PD, the player's cooperate decision tracks the opponent's previous-round move: P(cooperate | opp cooperated last round) > P(cooperate | opp defected last round). Operationalized as a one-sided Fisher exact contrast between those two conditional rates. Previously a Pearson correlation between prev_opp_coop_pd and player_cooperate, which is undefined against a deterministic tit-for-tat opponent whenever the agent's policy is constant: it returned r=nan in every archived session and scored 0, including for an agent that cooperated after 100% of opponent cooperations. The headline reciprocity signature. NOTE: if the agent never elicits an opponent defection, one bin is empty and the signature is correctly reported untestable rather than failed.
signatures.bias_rationale: Against a fixed tit-for-tat opponent the agent faces a sequential decision problem, not a strategic game. With the 15-round horizon shown on screen, the payoff-maximizing policy cooperates in every round but the last and, after a defection, cooperates again at once, since retaliating costs R - P per round. Reciprocity (cooperating less after the opponent defects) therefore departs from the best response.

signatures.name: above_chance_coordination_bos
signatures.description: In BoS, the player matches the opponent's action (lands on either equilibrium F-F or J-J) at a rate above chance (0.5). Camerer 2003 reports humans converge to 0.55+ within 10 rounds against alternating bots.

signatures.name: cooperation_when_opp_cooperated
signatures.description: Conditional cooperation: in PD rounds where the opponent (TFT bot) cooperated in the previous round, the player's cooperation rate is significantly above 0.5. This is the directional version of the reciprocity test - it asks 'when the opponent's last move was C, do you cooperate above chance?' Humans answer yes; random agents (~0.5 in any conditional bin) do not. Replaces the original non_zero_cooperation_pd signature which had a non-discriminative threshold (random cooperation ~0.5 trivially passes any threshold below 0.5).

signatures.name: round_rt_speedup
signatures.description: Response time falls across rounds as the game structure becomes familiar.
